# We'll Remind You Before Your Trial Ends

## Trial users who forget to cancel now get a heads-up before they're charged

¶1 **[City], [Date]** — [Company] today announced trial-ending reminders, a new notification system that alerts trial users before their subscription renews. Starting [date], users who signed up for a free trial will receive a reminder email three days before they're charged, giving them time to decide whether to continue or cancel. The change addresses a pattern where users who stopped using the product early in their trial were surprised by charges at the end of the trial period.

¶2 **The problem:** "I signed up for the free trial and tried it a few times in the first couple of days. Then I got busy and forgot about it. Two weeks later I saw a charge on my card and had no idea what it was for — I honestly thought it was fraud at first. When I realized it was [product], I felt tricked. I never would have let it renew if I'd remembered." That's the story behind 38% of the company's refund requests last quarter `[OBSERVED: refund log]`. "Surprise charge" is the #1 support ticket category in week 3 of every trial cohort `[OBSERVED: support ticket tags]`. Of users who eventually request refunds, 71% never opened the app after day 3 of their trial `[OBSERVED: activity × billing join]`. Reviews from refunders use words like "tricked" and "scam" `[REPORTED: review verbatims via support lead]`.

¶3 **The solution:** Three days before a trial ends, users receive an email with the subject line "Your trial ends in 3 days." The email states the exact date and amount they'll be charged, with a prominent one-click link to cancel if they don't want to continue. Users who are actively using the product see it as a helpful heads-up. Users who forgot about the trial get time to cancel before the charge hits their card. The reminder is sent only once per trial, and users can opt out of future reminders in their account settings.

¶4 **What exists today:** Trial users can see their billing date in their account settings, and the signup flow shows the trial terms. But users who try the product once and move on rarely check back. The current system relies on users remembering the exact date they signed up and doing calendar math to figure out when they'll be charged. Email confirmations mention the trial terms in a paragraph near the bottom `[NEEDS EVIDENCE: confirmation email open rate]`. For users who do get charged and want to cancel, the company offers refunds, but the request requires emailing support, waiting for a response, and explaining the situation. The refund is processed, but the user's experience of the brand is already damaged `[ASSUMED: causal link between surprise charges and negative brand perception]`. [NEEDS EVIDENCE: what % of trial users check their account settings after day 3]. The number of charged users who are unhappy but never request a refund — the "silent-angry" cohort — is not currently tracked `[UNKNOWN: C7]`.

¶5 **How we got here:** The company's internal debate centered on whether reminders would reduce trial-to-paid conversion `[ASSUMED: C5 — finance's concern, not yet measured]`. The assumption that bad reviews hurt conversion also lacks supporting data `[ASSUMED: C6]`. But the refund pattern was clear enough to act on, even without knowing the total cost of surprise charges to the business `[NEEDS EVIDENCE: cost of processing refunds vs. cost of reminder infrastructure, impact on lifetime value]`.

¶6 **What customers say:**

[Illustrative construction] "I got the reminder email two days before my trial ended and realized I'd completely forgotten I signed up. I wasn't using it, so I canceled right there. Way better than finding a mystery charge on my statement later."

"We don't want anyone to feel surprised or tricked," said [Spokesperson, Title]. "These reminders are about transparency. If someone tries our product and decides it's not for them, we want them to have an easy path out before they're charged. The users who love the product don't need the reminder, but they're not bothered by it either. And for people who forgot — this prevents the awful experience of a surprise charge. Auto-renewal regulations are tightening in several markets `[OBSERVED: public regulatory categories]`, and this puts us ahead of that curve while doing right by our users. We're moving on this now because the refund data showed us we had a real problem — when more than a third of your refunds come from people who say they forgot, that's worth fixing."

¶7 **Getting started:** Trial-ending reminders will roll out to all new trial users starting [date]. Existing trial users who signed up before [date] will receive reminders if their trial end date is more than three days away at launch. Users can manage their notification preferences at [URL]. Developers interested in the technical implementation can review the reminder-scheduling logic and email templates in [documentation link].

stages.output:
# 02-faq-internal.md — Internal

## Revenue & Finance

**Q: What's the revenue hit if this works exactly as intended?**  
OPEN — blocked on experiment design. We don't know how many reminder recipients will cancel who would have converted silently. Finance's model assumes 20-30% of current trial-to-paid conversions are forgot-cohort conversions we'll lose. Product believes most of those users wouldn't have stuck past the first paid month anyway, making them negative LTV once refund handling costs are included. The experiment will measure both immediate conversion impact and 90-day retention among reminder recipients vs. control.  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: If we lose 25% of trial conversions, how many quarters until the "better reviews" thesis pays back the revenue gap?**  
OPEN — blocked on attribution model. We claim bad reviews cost us conversions (¶2, ASSUMED — C6) but have never measured it. Even if we instrument review-to-signup attribution post-launch, we won't have a causal counterfactual. Finance wants a committed payback model before launch.  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: What do we show investors when Q2 trial conversion rate drops 20% and we're saying it's intentional?**  
OPEN — blocked on investor comms plan. If the experiment confirms conversion loss, do we have board approval to ship anyway? What's the threshold where we kill this despite the CX win?  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: The forgot-cohort is 71% of refunders — what percentage of total conversions are they?**  
OPEN — blocked on cohort segmentation. We know they're 71% of people who request refunds, but what's the denominator? If they're 5% of conversions, this is a rounding error. If they're 40%, it's a business model question.  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: What's our refund rate as a percentage of revenue, and how does it compare to industry benchmarks for our product category?**  
OPEN — no baseline. We track absolute refund volume but haven't calculated refund rate as % of billed revenue or benchmarked it. If we're at 2% and industry is 8%, maybe we don't have a problem worth risking conversion rate for.  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: "I felt scammed" (¶6) — is that illustrative construction or a real quote? If it's illustrative, what do the real verbatims say?**  
ANSWERED — ¶6 footer confirms illustrative construction. Real verbatims from review logs and support tickets use "tricked," "didn't know," "forgot I signed up," and "surprise charge" (¶2, OBSERVED). The illustrative quote synthesizes sentiment, not a literal customer statement.

**Q: One-tap cancel — what stops a user from mistapping and losing their trial data?**  
OPEN — blocked on UX confirmation flow. Does one-tap mean literally one tap, or one tap to a confirmation modal? If there's no confirmation, we'll generate support volume from accidental cancellations. If there is confirmation, it's not actually one tap.  
→ BLOCKER

## Legal & Compliance

**Q: Do current trial terms require notice before billing? If yes, are we already in breach? If no, why are we doing this?**  
OPEN — blocked on terms review. Legal needs to confirm whether existing terms obligate us to notify before conversion. If they do and we're not doing it, this isn't a "nice to have" feature, it's remediation. If they don't, what's the liability posture change from voluntarily adding notice?  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: What happens when a user claims they never received the reminder email and demands a refund?**  
OPEN — blocked on policy definition. Do we refund based on "didn't receive" claims even if logs show delivery? What's the process when their email provider blocked it? Does this create a new liability class where we're on the hook for email deliverability?  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: "Cancelling takes one tap, no retention maze" (¶1) — are we committing to never adding a retention flow, or is this a launch promise that can change later?**  
OPEN — blocked on policy lock-in. If this is a permanent commitment, it should be in terms. If it's a current-state description, what prevents us from adding "Are you sure?" or "Here's 50% off" flows in six months? If we add them later, do we re-trigger the "tricked" problem?  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: If a user cancels via one-tap but keeps using the product during the remaining trial, do they lose access immediately or at trial end?**  
OPEN — blocked on cancellation logic. Immediate shutoff will generate "I cancelled by accident" tickets. Access-until-trial-end means we're still providing service to someone who cancelled, which might confuse "when does my subscription actually end" for paid users.  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: Are we changing refund policy, or just reducing the volume of refund requests?**  
OPEN — blocked on policy definition. Does this change our obligation or willingness to refund "forgot to cancel" claims? If we send a reminder and they ignore it, can we deny the refund request? If yes, Legal needs to draft the new refund policy. If no, what's the business case if refund rate stays the same?  
→ BLOCKER

## Operations & Support

**Q: "Surprise charge" is #1 support category in week 3 (¶2) — what percentage of support volume is that, and where does it go after we ship this?**  
OPEN — blocked on capacity planning. If it's 30% of tickets and we cut it to 5%, do we reduce support headcount, or do those hours get backfilled by new issue categories? If new categories emerge (accidental cancellations, "didn't get reminder," "want trial extended"), have we just traded one support problem for three others?  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: What's the support SLA for "I didn't receive the reminder email"?**  
OPEN — blocked on playbook. Support needs a script, an escalation path, and authority to extend trials or issue refunds when delivery fails. Who owns the decision when a user's spam filter blocked our email?  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: The in-app banner — does it show once, or until dismissed, or on every session until trial ends?**  
OPEN — blocked on UX spec. If it shows once and the user misses it, we're back to "didn't know." If it shows every session, it's nagware. If it shows until dismissed, what's the dismiss behavior — "don't show again" or "remind me tomorrow"?  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: What happens when the email reminder goes to spam and the user never opens the app to see the banner?**  
OPEN — blocked on failure-mode policy. Is the intent "we tried to notify" (satisfied by sending) or "we ensured notification" (requires delivery confirmation + app open)? If a user gets charged because both channels failed, do we refund?  
→ BLOCKER

## Data & Measurement

**Q: The experiment (¶7, REQ-D2) — what's the measurement plan, sample size, and decision criteria?**  
OPEN — blocked on experiment design document. What's the primary metric: immediate conversion rate, 90-day LTV, refund rate, NPS? What's the minimum detectable effect and confidence threshold? What happens if conversion drops 5% (acceptable?) vs. 25% (kill it?)?  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: "Whether those reviews cost us conversions is something we believe and have not measured" (¶2, ASSUMED — C6) — when do we measure it?**  
OPEN — blocked on attribution instrumentation. We're shipping a feature predicated on an unmeasured assumption. What's the plan to validate it post-launch? How long until we know if the review sentiment → conversion thesis is real?  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: How are we defining "stopped opening the app by day 3" to identify the forgot-cohort?**  
ANSWERED — ¶2 provenance cites "OBSERVED: activity × billing join," indicating this is derived from session logs joined to billing events. Operational definition likely: zero app opens in days 4–14 of trial, followed by charge + refund request. Exact query should be documented in data dictionary.

**Q: 38% of refunds cite "forgot to cancel" — how are we tagging that? Free-text analysis, or a structured reason field?**  
ANSWERED — ¶2 cites "OBSERVED: refund log," and ¶2's support category data cites "ticket tags," suggesting structured categorization. Validation: can we reproduce the 38% figure from raw logs, or is it a support-team manual classification that might drift?

**Q: What's the false-positive rate on "forgot-cohort" identification? Are we reminding power users who just didn't open the app for two days?**  
OPEN — blocked on segmentation precision. If someone signs up, uses the app heavily on days 1-2, then doesn't open it days 3-14, do they get the reminder? What about users who have the app open but inactive (background state)? We risk annoying engaged users with unnecessary reminders.  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: If we're experimenting on reminder efficacy (REQ-D2), are we also experimenting on one-tap cancel placement, email copy, or timing (2 days before charge)?**  
OPEN — blocked on experiment scope. Is the experiment "reminders vs. no reminders," or are we also testing multi-variate on message content, timing, and cancel friction? If the experiment shows no conversion impact, will we know whether it's because reminders don't matter, or because our reminder execution was poor?  
→ BLOCKER

## Security & Fraud

**Q: One-tap cancel from email — what prevents someone from forwarding the email to cancel someone else's trial?**  
OPEN — blocked on authentication scheme. Does the email link require login, or is it a signed token? If it's a token, what's the expiration window and replay protection? If it requires login, it's not actually one-tap from email.  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: What stops a malicious actor from scraping trial emails and auto-cancelling them to grief our conversion rate?**  
OPEN — blocked on abuse mitigation. If cancel links are unauthenticated or use predictable tokens, we're exposed. If they require login, we need rate limiting and fraud detection. Have we threat-modeled this?  
→ BLOCKER

## Cross-Functional

**Q: "Receipts now show the next renewal date, every time" (¶1) — are we changing receipt content only, or also the billing system's renewal scheduling logic?**  
OPEN — blocked on implementation scope. If we're just surfacing existing renewal data, this is a template change. If renewal dates aren't currently deterministic (e.g., billing system recalculates on each cycle), we might be committing to something the system can't guarantee.  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: What's the rollout plan if the experiment shows a 15% conversion drop — ship it anyway, kill it, or iterate?**  
OPEN — blocked on decision authority and criteria. Who decides, and what's the threshold? If we kill it after the press release (¶1–8 written as if it's shipping), do we issue a retraction?  
→ BLOCKER

**Q: The current "fix" is refunds (¶4) — if this feature reduces refund requests by 60%, what's the cost savings vs. the conversion revenue loss?**  
OPEN — blocked on cost model. What's the fully-loaded cost per refund (support time, payment processing fees, churn risk)? If refunds cost us $8 each and we process 10,000/month, that's $80K/month in overhead. How many lost conversions can we absorb before the math breaks?  
→ BLOCKER

---

**Summary**: 24 questions. 4 ANSWERED. 20 OPEN (all tagged BLOCKER).  
This is not a "should we build it" document. This is a "what do we need to know before we can responsibly ship it" document. If Internal FAQ has zero blockers, the interrogation wasn't hostile enough.

# Demo Specification — The Surprise Charge

## Screens and surfaces

### S1. Email reminder (T-48h before first charge)
**Source:** PR ¶3  
**When:** Two days before trial converts to paid  
**Who sees it:** Every trial user at T-48h  
**Contains:**
- Subject: "Your trial ends in 2 days"
- Body: Current plan name, charge amount, charge date
- Two buttons: "Keep subscription" (confirms), "Cancel now" (one-tap cancel)
- If email send fails or lands late → see failure state F1

### S2. In-app banner (T-48h before first charge)
**Source:** PR ¶3  
**When:** User opens app between T-48h and charge  
**Who sees it:** Every trial user who opens app in that window  
**Contains:**
- Banner at top: "Your trial ends in 2 days — $X/month starts [DATE]"
- Two buttons: "Keep it" (dismisses), "Cancel subscription" (one-tap cancel)
- If banner doesn't render → see failure state F2

### S3. Receipt email (after successful charge)
**Source:** PR ¶5  
**When:** Immediately after charge completes  
**Contains:**
- Receipt line items
- **New:** Next renewal date and amount, displayed prominently
- One-tap "Manage subscription" link
- Current receipts don't show next renewal → this adds it

### S4. One-tap cancellation confirmation
**Source:** PR ¶3, ¶5  
**When:** User taps cancel from email, banner, or receipt  
**Contains:**
- "Your subscription is cancelled"
- "You won't be charged on [DATE]"
- No retention maze, no additional steps
- If cancellation API fails → see failure state F3

### S5. Account settings (unchanged, for comparison)
**Source:** PR ¶4  
**Current state:** Renewal date shown, requires user to navigate to settings  
**Problem:** Users who stopped opening app never see it  
**This demo shows:** Why settings-only disclosure fails the forgot-cohort

---

## Primary flow

### Flow A: Inactive trial user (the forgot-cohort)

1. **Day 1** — User starts trial, uses app
2. **Day 3** — User stops opening app
3. **Day 12 (T-48h)** — User receives email reminder [S1]
   - Sees: Subject "Your trial ends in 2 days", charge amount $X, two buttons
4. **User taps "Cancel now"** from email
5. **Immediately** — Sees confirmation [S4]: "Your subscription is cancelled. You won't be charged on [DATE]"
6. **Day 14** — No charge occurs, no surprise, no angry review

### Flow B: Active trial user who wants to keep it

1. **Day 1** — User starts trial, uses app regularly
2. **Day 12 (T-48h)** — User opens app, sees banner [S2]
   - Banner: "Your trial ends in 2 days — $9/month starts April 16"
3. **User taps "Keep it"** — banner dismisses
4. **Day 14** — Charge succeeds
5. **Immediately** — Receives receipt [S3] showing: "Next renewal: May 16, 2027 — $9"
6. **Outcome** — User knows exactly when next charge happens

### Flow C: User who ignores reminder, then changes mind

1. **Day 12** — Receives email [S1], doesn't act
2. **Day 13** — Opens app, sees banner [S2], ignores it
3. **Day 14** — Charge succeeds, receives receipt [S3]
4. **User opens receipt** — sees "Next renewal: May 16, 2027"
5. **User taps "Manage subscription"** from receipt
6. **User taps "Cancel subscription"** — one tap [S4]
7. **Sees confirmation** — "You won't be charged on May 16"
8. **Outcome** — Cancels after first charge, but wasn't surprised by it

---

## Failure states

| What fails | Exactly what user sees | Source | Severity |
|------------|------------------------|--------|----------|
| Email doesn't send (queue failure, bounce) | No email arrives at T-48h; banner [S2] is fallback, but user must open app | BLK-05 | HIGH |
| Email sends late (after charge) | Email arrives post-charge; user already charged, defeats purpose | BLK-05 | CRITICAL |
| Banner doesn't render (client bug, A/B test bucketing error) | User who opens app sees nothing; email [S1] is fallback if it landed | Implementation risk | MEDIUM |
| Cancellation API fails (vendor webhook timeout, network error) | User taps cancel → sees "Something went wrong, try again" with retry button; cancellation NOT confirmed | Implementation risk | HIGH |
| User has no email on file | No email sent; banner [S2] is only notification; if user doesn't open app, silent failure | Data quality risk | MEDIUM |
| Billing runs before T-48h window opens (clock skew, vendor time mismatch) | User charged with zero notice; entire feature bypassed | BLK-05 | CRITICAL |

**Key invariant from rules:** "Silence never renders as success." If reminder doesn't send, and user doesn't open app → banner never shows → user gets charged without warning → FAILURE STATE, not silent success.

---

## What this deliberately does NOT show

### 1. The holdback experiment (REQ-D2)
**Why not:** Demo shows the treatment experience. The experiment's control group (no reminders) and the revenue readout (does this cost conversions?) are measurement apparatus, not user-facing screens.  
**Blocker:** None — this is in scope for telemetry (05-telemetry.md), not demo.  
**Boundary:** Demo shows one trial user's journey; experiment shows 10,000 users' aggregate conversion rates.

### 2. How the T-48h timing guarantee works
**Why not:** The demo assumes email lands T-48h before charge. The platform work to guarantee that (webhook ordering, queue monitoring, alerting when delivery lags) is infrastructure, not a screen.  
**Blocker:** BLK-05 (DEPENDENCY, severity medium) — "Who owns the guarantee that T-48h means T-48h?"  
**Boundary:** Demo shows "email arrives 2 days early"; implementation shows "this is how we make that true."

### 3. The silent churners measurement
**Why not:** PR ¶2 says 71% of refunders are forgot-cohort; IFAQ-03 asks about users who churn silently (charged, surprised, quit, never complain). Measuring them is a data join, not a demo moment.  
**Blocker:** BLK-04 (DATA, severity medium) — "How many charged users are surprised and silent?"  
**Boundary:** Demo shows the refunder's alternate path (cancel before charge); analytics shows how many never complained but left anyway.

### 4. Legal review of past charges and regulatory requirements
**Why not:** IFAQ-04 raises two questions: (a) what does announcing this say about charges we already took, (b) do some markets already require this notice? Both are legal review, not user experience.  
**Blocker:** BLK-03 (LEGAL, severity high) — past charges framing; BLK-02 (REGULATORY) — compliance requirements.  
**Boundary:** Demo shows the experience we're building; legal review shows whether we're allowed to build it (and what we say about the past).

### 5. Finance approval and revenue impact modeling
**Why not:** IFAQ-01 asks how much revenue reminders cost. That's a spreadsheet finance builds after the experiment reads out, not a screen.  
**Blocker:** BLK-01 (COMMERCIAL, severity high) — "Are you asking me to approve a number you can't state?"  
**Boundary:** Demo shows the reminder; finance shows whether the company can afford to send it.

### 6. Engagement-washing prevention (open rates vs actual surprise reduction)
**Why not:** IFAQ-05 asks what stops this from being "big open rates, no fewer angry customers." The north-star metric (surprises, not opens) is telemetry design, not a demo screen.  
**Blocker:** None — telemetry design is in scope for 05-telemetry.md.  
**Boundary:** Demo shows the reminder and cancellation; metrics show whether it actually reduced "surprise charge" support tickets.

---

## Affected personas

### Persona: Inactive trial user (the forgot-cohort)

**Today (before):**
- Signs up, tries app, stops using it by day 3
- Gets charged on day 14 with zero warning
- Discovers charge on bank statement
- Feels scammed, writes angry review: "I didn't even remember signing up"
- Contacts support, gets refund
- Review stays; never comes back

**After (with reminders):**
- Same start: signs up, tries app, stops by day 3
- Day 12: receives email "Your trial ends in 2 days"
- Taps "Cancel now" (one tap)
- Sees confirmation: "You won't be charged on [DATE]"
- Day 14: no charge, no surprise, no angry review
- **Outcome:** Clean exit instead of refund cycle

---

## The ask

**To finance (BLK-01):** Approve the holdback experiment. If reminders cost conversions, we'll measure it. If they don't, we stopped charging people who were going to refund anyway.

**To platform (BLK-05):** Own the T-48h guarantee. Billing webhook and email queue are separate vendors; someone must ensure email lands before charge or this fails silently.

**To legal (BLK-03, BLK-02):** Review both halves: (a) framing for past charges, (b) whether some markets already required this notice. The second half changes this from "improvement" to "remediation."

**To analytics (BLK-04):** Measure the silent churners (charged → no activity → month 2 churn, no ticket). They're the ones who didn't complain but left anyway — and they decide how big this problem actually is.

**To product leadership:** Ship the reminder with the experiment that settles the revenue question. Every surprise charge is revenue this quarter and a detractor forever. This demo shows we'd rather earn the conversion than ambush it.

---

**Provenance:** 3 observed · 1 reported · 1 assumed · the conversion question is REQ-D2's experiment  
**Blockers unresolved:** BLK-01, BLK-02, BLK-03, BLK-04, BLK-05  
**Screens specified:** 5 · Flows specified: 3 · Failure states: 6

# Trial Reminder — Customer Documentation

## What it does

Before your trial converts to a paid plan, we'll remind you. Two days before your first charge, you'll get an email and see a banner in the app. Both give you two options: keep your plan, or cancel in one tap.

Every receipt shows your next renewal date and the amount we'll charge.

## Before you start

Nothing. This works automatically for all trials. You don't need to enable it or change any settings.

## How it works

### When your trial is about to end

**Two days before your first charge**, you'll get:
- An email with the subject line `[UNKNOWN — BLK-D1: email subject not specified]`
- A banner at the top of the app

Both show:
- The date we'll charge you
- The amount
- Two buttons: **Keep my plan** or **Cancel now**

### If you want to keep your plan

Click **Keep my plan**, or do nothing. Your plan continues and we'll charge you on the date shown.

### If you want to cancel

Click **Cancel now** from the reminder email, the in-app banner, or your account settings. You won't be charged.

Cancelling takes one tap. You won't see surveys, discount offers, or multiple confirmation screens. The number of steps to cancel will never exceed the number of steps it took to start your trial. *(Requirement: REQ-DP5)*

### After you're charged

Every receipt shows:
- The amount charged
- The date of your next renewal
- `[UNKNOWN — BLK-D2: does the receipt also include a cancel link? Source: PR ¶5 mentions "cancel from receipt" but mechanism unclear]`

## Limits

| What | Limit | Why |
|------|-------|-----|
| Who gets reminders | Trial users only | Existing paid users already know their renewal date |
| How many reminders | One per trial | `[UNKNOWN — BLK-D3: what if trial extends? Or if user restarts trial later?]` |
| When you'll be reminded | 2 days before first charge | Fixed timing |
| Reminder delivery | Email + in-app banner | `[UNKNOWN — BLK-D4: SMS? Push notification? What if email bounces?]` |
| Languages | `[UNKNOWN — BLK-D5: localization status unclear]` | `[UNKNOWN]` |
| Grace period after first charge | `[UNKNOWN — BLK-D6: can you cancel immediately after being charged for a refund?]` | `[UNKNOWN]` |

## Troubleshooting

### Could not be written yet

The following sections require information not yet available:

**What you'll see when it fails**
- **Blocker BLK-D7**: No demo spec exists yet. Need failure scenarios: email doesn't arrive, banner doesn't show, cancel button doesn't work, wrong date displayed, reminder sent to wrong cohort.

**Troubleshooting scenarios**
- **Blocker BLK-D8**: Error messages not specified. What does the user see if cancel fails? If email bounces? If they're in a state the system doesn't expect (e.g., trial already expired but no charge yet)?

**Edge cases**
- **Blocker BLK-D9**: What if the user is offline when banner should appear?
- **Blocker BLK-D10**: What if payment method is already invalid when we try to charge?
- **Blocker BLK-D11**: User cancels, then changes their mind before trial ends — can they un-cancel?
- **Blocker BLK-D12**: Trial user was already surprise-charged in the past, before this shipped. Do they get anything? (Connected to EFAQ-04, BLK-03)

**Time zone handling**
- **Blocker BLK-D13**: "2 days before" in which time zone? User's? Company's? What if user changes time zones during trial?

**"The app" definition**
- **Blocker BLK-D14**: Which app/product is this? Where exactly does the banner appear? What if there are multiple products under one account?

### Common issues — draft

| Problem | Solution | Status |
|---------|----------|--------|
| I didn't get the email | `[Check spam folder? → BLK-D8]` | Cannot complete |
| The banner isn't showing | `[Refresh? Relog? → BLK-D8]` | Cannot complete |
| I clicked cancel but was still charged | `[Contact support? Automatic refund? → BLK-D8]` | Cannot complete |
| The renewal date shown was wrong | `[What's the escalation path? → BLK-D8]` | Cannot complete |

---

## Document blockers summary

**7 blockers prevent completion**:
- BLK-D1: Email subject line not specified
- BLK-D2: Receipt cancel mechanism unclear (PR ¶5 mentions it but no detail)
- BLK-D7: No demo spec = no failure documentation
- BLK-D8: Error messages and user-facing troubleshooting steps undefined
- BLK-D13: Time zone handling not specified
- BLK-D14: Product/app identity unclear (generic "the app")

**6 limits questions need answers**:
- BLK-D3: Behavior for extended/restarted trials
- BLK-D4: Email delivery failure handling, alternative channels
- BLK-D5: Localization status
- BLK-D6: Post-charge cancellation/refund policy
- BLK-D9: Offline banner behavior
- BLK-D10: Invalid payment method handling
- BLK-D11: Un-cancel flow
- BLK-D12: Retroactive refunds for past surprise charges (connects to EFAQ-04/BLK-03)

**Core documentation is draftable** (what/how/limits structure) but **cannot be shipped** without failure modes, error messages, and edge case handling.

stages.name: Telemetry

props.desc: a north star is named
metrics cite the claims they guard
at least one [UNKNOWN] baseline (inputs guarantee one exists)
the unmeasurable list / instrument-or-cut section exists

stages.output:
# 05-telemetry.md

## North star

**Forgot-cohort charge rate**: % of trial users who (a) were inactive for the final 7 days of trial AND (b) converted to paid.

- **Measures**: ¶2's core problem — "the trial user who stopped opening the app by day 3 and gets charged on day 14 anyway"
- **Denominator rule**: All trial starts, not just conversions. The system sees only those who convert; the full cohort includes those who cancelled or let the trial lapse.
- **Gaming rule**: Killing the reminder email would reduce this number (fewer inactive users convert) without creating value. Guard: measure separately as an input metric (conversion rate); the experiment in REQ-D2 exists to catch this exact gaming vector.
- **Current baseline**: [UNKNOWN] — requires join of activity log (last-open timestamp) and billing events (trial-to-paid conversion). Instrumentation exists for both tables; query does not.

---

## Input metrics

### M1: Forgot-cohort share of refunds
**Claim**: ¶2 — "71% of our eventual refunders"  
**Definition**: Of users who request a refund in their first billing period, % who were inactive for the final 7 days of trial  
**Baseline**: 71% `[OBSERVED: activity × billing join]` — documented as observed, query provenance unknown  
**Instrumentation point**: Refund request handler + activity log join  
**Exists today**: [UNKNOWN] — the 71% figure exists, but whether the join is instrumented as a standing query is unverified  
**Owner question**: Is the 71% figure from a one-time analysis or a dashboard? If one-time, instrument as recurring metric.

### M2: "Forgot to cancel" refund reason share
**Claim**: ¶2 — "38% of last quarter's refunds cite 'forgot to cancel'"  
**Definition**: % of refund requests in period whose reason field matches `forgot|didn't know|surprise|didn't realize` (case-insensitive)  
**Baseline**: 38% (Q4 2026) `[OBSERVED: refund log]`  
**Instrumentation point**: Refund request submission (reason field capture)  
**Exists today**: YES — refund log captures free-text reason  
**Note**: Text matching is brittle. Consider structured reason taxonomy.

### M3: Week-3 support load, "surprise charge" category
**Claim**: ¶2 — "'surprise charge' is the #1 support category in week three of every cohort"  
**Definition**: Count of tickets tagged `surprise-charge` OR `billing-confusion` filed 15–21 days post-trial-start, as % of cohort  
**Baseline**: [UNKNOWN] — claim states it is #1 category but not the absolute rate  
**Instrumentation point**: Support ticket creation (tags + trial cohort join)  
**Exists today**: PARTIAL — ticket tags exist, cohort join unknown  
**Owner question**: What is the actual rate (tickets per 100 trial starts) for week 3? We know it's #1 but not whether it's 2% or 20%.

### M4: Conversion rate (trial → paid)
**Claim**: ¶7 (implicit) — "finance believes reminders will cost us conversions"  
**Definition**: % of trial starts that convert to a paid plan at trial end  
**Baseline**: [UNKNOWN]  
**Instrumentation point**: Billing system (trial start event + conversion event)  
**Exists today**: YES — this is a core business metric, assumed instrumented  
**Note**: This is the countervailing metric. If north star (forgot-cohort charge rate) falls but M4 also falls, the intervention failed. REQ-D2's experiment exists to measure this tradeoff.

### M5: Reminder delivery + interaction rate
**Claim**: ¶3 — "Two days before the first charge, we tell you — an email and an in-app banner"  
**Definition**: 
  - M5a: % of trial users who reach T-2 days and receive the reminder email (sent successfully)
  - M5b: % of reminder recipients who open the email
  - M5c: % of reminder recipients who click "keep it" or "cancel" from email
  - M5d: % of trial users who see the in-app banner (banner impression logged)
  - M5e: % of banner viewers who tap "keep it" or "cancel"  
**Baseline**: [UNKNOWN] — new feature, no prior baseline  
**Instrumentation point**: 
  - Email send queue + delivery webhook (M5a/b)
  - Email click tracker (M5c)
  - Client-side analytics (banner impression, M5d)
  - Client-side analytics (banner tap, M5e)  
**Exists today**: NO — requires new instrumentation for banner, email click tracking may exist  
**Owner question**: Does email platform support click tracking today? Does mobile/web client send custom event logging?

### M6: One-tap cancel completion rate
**Claim**: ¶5 — "Cancelling is one tap from the reminder, the banner, or the receipt"  
**Definition**: Of users who initiate cancel from (reminder email | in-app banner | receipt), % who complete cancellation without additional steps  
**Baseline**: [UNKNOWN] — defines the new behavior  
**Instrumentation point**: Cancel flow entry (source: email/banner/receipt) + cancel flow completion  
**Exists today**: PARTIAL — cancel completion likely instrumented, source attribution unknown  
**Owner question**: Can we attribute cancel source today (email vs. banner vs. receipt vs. settings)?

### M7: Receipt views
**Claim**: ¶5 — "Receipts state the next renewal date and price"  
**Definition**: % of paid users who view a receipt within 7 days of charge  
**Baseline**: [UNKNOWN]  
**Instrumentation point**: Receipt page view or email open (if receipts are emailed)  
**Exists today**: [UNKNOWN] — depends on whether receipts are web views (logged) or plain email (open-tracking)  
**Owner question**: Are receipts HTML emails with open tracking, or PDF attachments, or web views? Instrumentation differs.

---

## Unmeasurable list

### U1: Review sentiment cost to conversions
**Claim**: ¶2 — "Whether those reviews cost us conversions is something we believe and have not measured"  
**Status**: ASSUMED (C6 in provenance)  
**Decision required**: 
  - **Option A**: Instrument review-exposure-to-conversion funnel (requires cohort of users who viewed app store page, join with install/trial-start). High instrumentation cost.
  - **Option B**: Accept as assumed and move forward. The reviews are real; whether they suppress conversions by 1% or 10% does not change the decision to fix the root cause.
  - **Option C**: Cut the claim from ¶2. It is narrative color, not load-bearing.  
**Recommendation**: Option B. The harm (bad reviews) is observable. The conversion impact is plausible but hard to measure and not necessary to justify the fix.

### U2: "Reviews say 'tricked'" — quantified prevalence
**Claim**: ¶2 — "their reviews say 'tricked'"  
**Status**: REPORTED (review verbatims) but not quantified  
**Decision required**:
  - **Option A**: Run sentiment analysis on app store reviews (filter to first-billing-period users, keyword match or LLM tag for "tricked | scammed | didn't know | surprise"). Report as "X% of reviews from first-month users mention surprise charges."
  - **Option B**: Keep as qualitative signal (anecdotal). The 38% refund-reason figure (M2) measures the same underlying issue quantitatively.
  - **Option C**: Cut the claim.  
**Recommendation**: Option B. M2 already quantifies the problem. Sentiment analysis is a nice-to-have, not a blocker.

### U3: "One tap" — what is the current cancel flow step count?
**Claim**: ¶5 — "Cancelling is one tap from the reminder... never more steps than subscribing took"  
**Status**: Comparative claim (new flow vs. old flow, new flow vs. subscribe flow) but no baseline step count stated  
**Decision required**:
  - **Option A**: Document current cancel flow step count (manual QA: count taps from settings → cancellation confirmed). Document subscribe flow step count. Commit to new flow being ≤ subscribe flow.
  - **Option B**: Reframe claim as absolute ("one tap from reminder") and drop the comparative clause.  
**Recommendation**: Option A. The "never more steps than subscribing" clause is a specific, testable promise. Measure it before and after. Deliver as QA checklist, not telemetry.

---

## Owner questions requiring baseline data

1. **M1 query provenance**: The 71% figure is documented as observed. Is this from a standing dashboard or a one-time analysis? If one-time, who can write the recurring query?
2. **M3 absolute rate**: We know "surprise charge" is the #1 week-3 category. What is the rate per 100 trial starts?
3. **M4 current conversion rate**: Trial → paid conversion % (last quarter). Assumed instrumented; verify with Finance or Growth.
4. **M5 email click tracking**: Does the email platform support click tracking today, or does it need to be added?
5. **M5 client-side events**: Do mobile/web clients send custom events for banner impressions and taps, or does this require SDK instrumentation?
6. **M6 cancel source attribution**: Can we attribute cancel actions to their entry point (email link / in-app banner / receipt / settings page)?
7. **M7 receipt format and tracking**: Are receipts HTML emails (open-trackable), PDFs (not trackable), or web views (page-view trackable)?

---

## Instrumentation gaps (does not exist today)

- **M1**: Forgot-cohort charge rate as standing metric (if current 71% figure was one-time analysis)
- **M3**: Week-3 support load cohort join (ticket tags exist, cohort join unknown)
- **M5d/e**: In-app banner impression + tap tracking (requires client-side instrumentation)
- **M6**: Cancel source attribution (if not already captured)
- **M7**: Receipt view tracking (depends on format — may require new instrumentation)

---

## Summary

- **North star**: Forgot-cohort charge rate (% of trial cohort inactive in final 7 days who convert to paid). Baseline [UNKNOWN], requires activity × billing join query.
- **7 input metrics** defined; 3 have known baselines, 4 are [UNKNOWN] and routed to owners as questions.
- **3 unmeasurable claims** routed as forced decisions: review sentiment impact (recommend accept as assumed), review verbatim prevalence (recommend qualitative), cancel flow step count (recommend QA checklist, not telemetry).
- **7 owner questions** block baseline establishment.
- **5 instrumentation gaps** require engineering work before launch.

props.desc: >=3 requirements, every one with a Source: line
GIVEN/WHEN/THEN acceptance on at least 3 requirements
the [ASSUMED] chain is flagged RESTS ON ASSUMPTION

stages.output:
# 06 · Requirements

> Extracted from PR (rev after REVISE on dimension 1) and IFAQ tier-0 run.
> Every requirement cites its source. Flags appear inline.

---

## Core notification requirements

**REQ-D1 · Pre-charge email notification**  
Source: PR ¶3  
Statement: The system sends an email notification to trial users two days before their first charge, stating the charge date, amount, and offering one-tap keep/cancel actions.  
Acceptance criteria: GIVEN a trial user whose first charge is scheduled for day 14 / WHEN day 12 arrives (T-48h) / THEN an email is delivered to their registered address containing the charge date, amount, and two action buttons (keep subscription, cancel subscription)  
Out of scope: Multi-language variants, email client compatibility testing, notification history UI  
Depends on: BLK-05  
**⚠ SHAPE PENDING** — BLK-05 (cross-vendor timing guarantee) is OPEN. Fork: if billing/email timing cannot be guaranteed, requirement splits into best-effort notification + post-charge refund automation, or notification moves to in-app only with email as non-blocking courtesy.

---

**REQ-D2 · Pre-charge in-app banner**  
Source: PR ¶3  
Statement: The system displays an in-app banner to trial users two days before their first charge, stating the charge date, amount, and offering one-tap keep/cancel actions.  
Acceptance criteria: GIVEN a trial user whose first charge is scheduled for day 14 / WHEN they open the app on or after day 12 (T-48h) / THEN a banner appears in the main interface showing the charge date, amount, and two action buttons (keep subscription, cancel subscription), persisting until the user acts or the charge completes  
Out of scope: Banner placement/design specifics, cross-platform UI consistency, banner dismissal without action  
Depends on: BLK-05  
**⚠ SHAPE PENDING** — BLK-05 (cross-vendor timing guarantee) is OPEN. Same fork as REQ-D1.

---

**REQ-D3 · One-tap cancellation from reminder**  
Source: PR ¶3, PR ¶5  
Statement: The cancellation flow initiated from the pre-charge reminder (email or banner) completes in one user action with no retention prompts, surveys, or confirmation steps.  
Acceptance criteria: GIVEN a user viewing the pre-charge reminder email or banner / WHEN they tap/click the "cancel subscription" button / THEN their trial subscription is immediately cancelled, a confirmation message is shown, and no charge occurs on day 14, with zero additional taps/clicks required  
Out of scope: Post-cancellation feedback surveys (may be offered but not required), win-back campaigns, partial refunds  
Depends on: None

---

**REQ-D4 · Receipt displays next renewal date and amount**  
Source: PR ¶1, PR ¶5  
Statement: Every subscription charge receipt displays the next scheduled renewal date and charge amount.  
Acceptance criteria: GIVEN a user who has been charged for a subscription period / WHEN they view the receipt (email, in-app, or transaction history) / THEN the receipt text includes "Next charge: [YYYY-MM-DD] for [amount with currency]"  
Out of scope: Receipts for one-time purchases, prorated charges, tax breakdowns, receipt archival  
Depends on: None

---

**REQ-D5 · Cancellation step-count parity with signup**  
Source: PR ¶5  
Statement: The cancellation flow requires no more user actions than the subscription signup flow required.  
Acceptance criteria: GIVEN a subscription that was initiated in N taps (where N = count from trial signup button to confirmation screen) / WHEN a user cancels from any entry point (reminder, banner, receipt, settings) / THEN cancellation completes in ≤N taps with no intermediate retention screens, counter-offers, or "are you sure" dialogs  
Out of scope: Definition of N per platform (web/iOS/Android), accessibility action equivalents (voice, keyboard), step-counting methodology documentation  
Depends on: REQ-D3, REQ-D6

---

**REQ-D6 · One-tap cancellation from receipt**  
Source: PR ¶5  
Statement: Every subscription charge receipt provides a one-tap cancellation option.  
Acceptance criteria: GIVEN a user viewing a subscription charge receipt / WHEN they tap/click the cancellation link or button / THEN their subscription is immediately cancelled with confirmation, and no additional taps/clicks are required  
Out of scope: Refund initiation from receipt, partial-period refunds, receipt-based subscription management (pause, downgrade)  
Depends on: None

---

**REQ-D7 · Automatic enrollment of new trial cohorts**  
Source: PR ¶8  
Statement: The reminder system activates automatically for all trial users starting from the launch date, with no per-user, per-plan, or administrative configuration required.  
Acceptance criteria: GIVEN the feature has launched to production / WHEN a new trial user signs up on or after the launch date / THEN they are automatically enrolled in the pre-charge reminder flow (email + banner at T-48h) with no feature flag, admin toggle, or manual enablement step  
Out of scope: Backfilling reminders for in-flight trials started before launch, manual opt-out mechanisms, country/plan-specific rollout phasing  
Depends on: None

---

## Measurement & learning requirements

**REQ-D8 · Conversion impact holdback experiment**  
Source: PR ¶7, IFAQ-01  
Statement: The reminder system launches with a controlled experiment that measures conversion, refund, and revenue impact by comparing a treatment group (reminders enabled) against a holdback control group (no reminders, current experience).  
Acceptance criteria: GIVEN the feature launches / WHEN trial cohorts are randomly assigned to treatment (reminders) or control (no reminders) groups / THEN conversion rates, refund rates, refund reason distribution, support ticket volume, and net revenue are tracked per group and tested for statistical significance, with results available within one trial cycle (14 days) after minimum sample size is reached  
Out of scope: Experiment duration, sample size calculation, significance threshold (α), multivariate testing (e.g., reminder timing variants), long-term LTV measurement  
Depends on: BLK-01  
**⚠ RESTS ON ASSUMPTION** — C5 (finance belief: reminders reduce conversion) and C6 (author belief: negative reviews from surprise charges reduce conversion) are both untested. The experiment is designed to resolve this disagreement, but requirement approval depends on BLK-01 (commercial stakeholder accepting experiment risk).  
**⚠ SHAPE PENDING** — BLK-01 (commercial approval) is OPEN. Fork: if finance blocks the experiment, requirement becomes observational-only (treatment group only, no control) or feature is shelved pending alternate validation method.

---

**REQ-D9 · Surprise charge metric instrumentation**  
Source: IFAQ-05, PR ¶2  
Statement: The system instruments a "surprise charge" metric that counts trial-to-paid conversions where the user showed no activity in the 7 days preceding the charge.  
Acceptance criteria: GIVEN a trial user whose subscription converted to paid / WHEN their last in-app activity (session start, feature use, or settings access) occurred >7 days before the charge date / THEN the conversion event is tagged as "surprise_charge=true" in the data warehouse and appears in the surprise charge metric dashboard  
Out of scope: Real-time alerting on surprise charges, user-facing surprise charge indicator, predictive modeling of likely-surprised users  
Depends on: BLK-04  
**⚠ SHAPE PENDING** — BLK-04 (data pipeline for activity×billing join) is OPEN. Fork: if cross-source join is not feasible, requirement downgrades to refund-reason tagging only (reactive measure, not proactive cohort identification).

---

## Compliance & legal requirements

**REQ-D10 · Auto-renewal disclosure compliance**  
Source: IFAQ-04  
Statement: The pre-charge notification satisfies auto-renewal disclosure requirements in all markets where the product is sold.  
Acceptance criteria: GIVEN the product is available in markets with auto-renewal notification laws (e.g., California, EU member states) / WHEN a trial user in one of those markets reaches T-48h before their first charge / THEN the email and banner notifications include all legally mandated disclosures (renewal date, amount, cancellation method, contact information) in the format required by that jurisdiction  
Out of scope: Market-by-market legal review documentation, translation/localization, grandfathering of pre-launch users  
Depends on: BLK-02, BLK-03  
**⚠ SHAPE PENDING** — BLK-02 (regulatory requirements) and BLK-03 (legal implications of announcement) are OPEN. Fork: if legal review determines current practice is non-compliant in some markets, requirement elevates from "improvement" to "remediation" and may require user notification, refund campaign, or market-specific launch sequencing.

---

## Flagged requirements (no source found)

_None at this stage. All requirements trace to PR or IFAQ._

---

## Blockers affecting requirements above

- **BLK-01** · COMMERCIAL · severity high · Status: OPEN  
  Finance approval for conversion holdback experiment (REQ-D8)

- **BLK-02** · REGULATORY · severity unknown · Status: OPEN  
  Auto-renewal notification laws by market (REQ-D10)

- **BLK-03** · LEGAL · severity high · Status: OPEN  
  Legal implications of "trial that ends politely" announcement (REQ-D10)

- **BLK-04** · DATA · severity medium · Status: OPEN  
  Activity×billing join for silent churn measurement (REQ-D9)

- **BLK-05** · DEPENDENCY · severity medium · Status: OPEN  
  Cross-vendor timing guarantee (billing webhook + email queue) (REQ-D1, REQ-D2)

---

## Assumptions flagged in requirements

- **C5** — Finance belief that reminders reduce conversion (IFAQ-01, affects REQ-D8)
- **C6** — Author belief that negative reviews from surprise charges reduce conversion (PR ¶2, affects REQ-D8)
- **C7** — Unknown: volume of silent churners (charged users who are surprised but don't request refund) (IFAQ-03, affects problem sizing but no requirement yet depends on it)

---

**Next step:** `python scripts/verify_sources.py wb/<session-id>`

# Release Plan — The Surprise Charge

5 slices. 7 requirements assigned. 3 slices blocked.

---

## Slice 1: Instrumentation foundation

**Requirements:** REQ-D1

**Ships:** Surprise Rate dashboard showing per-cohort metrics (Surprise Rate, M4, cohort sizes) for US users. Join layer connecting charges, refunds, "surprise" tickets, and activity history.

**Proves:** We can measure the problem's size and track changes.

**Scenario:** Analytics team can answer "how many users are surprised" with confidence intervals.

**Dependencies:** None

**Blockers:** None

**Status:** SCHEDULABLE

---

## Slice 2: In-app awareness (no email dependency)

**Requirements:** REQ-DP2, REQ-DP4

**Ships:** 
- Day 12+ in-app banner showing charge date, price, keep/cancel actions (US only)
- Receipt redesign: every receipt shows next renewal date, next price, cancel link

**Proves:** Users who open the app learn about upcoming charges; every charge reminds about the next one.

**Scenario:** Trial user opens app on day 13, sees banner, decides to keep subscription with full knowledge of what's coming.

**Dependencies:** None

**Blockers:** None

**Status:** SCHEDULABLE

---

## Slice 3: One-tap cancel (US-first, per-market expansion)

**Requirements:** REQ-DP3, REQ-DP5

**Ships:** One-tap cancel flow for US market, respecting parity rule (cancel steps ≤ subscribe steps). CI assertion enforcing parity per market config. Data retained 30 days.

**Proves:** Cancelling can be easier than the current flow, and we can enforce parity automatically.

**Scenario:** User taps cancel from reminder/banner/receipt, sees inline confirmation on that screen, done.

**Dependencies:** None (can ship standalone; reminder/banner/receipt can link to it once each ships)

**Blockers:** BLK-02 — per-market cancel requirements unknown. Q-06 pending: do regulated markets prescribe a specific cancel method? Owner: Legal. Unblocking meeting: Legal/Product review (no date set).

**Status:** NOT SCHEDULABLE — blocked on BLK-02

**Per-market expansion:** Once unblocked, US ships first. Other markets follow as BLK-02 resolves per-market requirements. Each market config asserts parity in CI before deploy.

---

## Slice 4: Email reminder (T-48h)

**Requirements:** REQ-DP1

**Ships:** One email at day 12 (≥48h before day 14 charge), US only. States price, date. Offers keep/cancel with equal weight. Send failures logged and surfaced (never silent). M1 metric verifies 48h ordering.

**Proves:** We can reach users before the charge, outside the app.

**Scenario:** Trial user receives email on day 12, clicks "Keep my subscription" or "Cancel," acts before the charge.

**Dependencies:** Slice 1 (M1 measurement requires the join)

**Blockers:** BLK-05 — email infrastructure readiness unknown. Owner: Platform Engineering. Unblocking meeting: Email capability review (no date set).

**Status:** NOT SCHEDULABLE — blocked on BLK-05

---

## Slice 5: The reminder holdback experiment

**Requirements:** REQ-D2

**Ships:** Randomized holdback experiment: control cohort receives no reminder, treatment receives Slice 4 reminder. Day-60 readout compares net revenue, states effect size, confidence interval, cohort sizes. If underpowered, declares that rather than extending silently.

**Proves:** Whether reminders help or hurt net revenue (addresses C5 — the finance fear).

**Scenario:** Product and Finance review day-60 readout, decide whether to roll out reminders based on measured revenue impact.

**Dependencies:** Slice 1 (measurement), Slice 4 (the reminder being tested)

**Blockers:** BLK-01 — Finance must co-own experiment design, or readout settles nothing. Owner: Finance. Unblocking meeting: Finance/Product experiment design review (no date set).

**Status:** NOT SCHEDULABLE — blocked on BLK-01

**Shape pending:** Experiment parameters (sample size, randomization unit, holdback percentage) to be determined when BLK-01 resolves.

---

## Dependency DAG


S1 (Instrumentation)
 ├─→ S4 (Email reminder) [blocked: BLK-05]
 └─→ S5 (Experiment) [blocked: BLK-01]

S2 (In-app awareness)
  [no dependencies]

S3 (One-tap cancel) [blocked: BLK-02]
  [no dependencies, but reminder/banner/receipt link to it once each ships]

S4 (Email reminder) [blocked: BLK-05]
 └─→ S5 (Experiment) [blocked: BLK-01]

**Edge list:**
- S1 → S4
- S1 → S5
- S4 → S5

**Acyclic:** Yes. Critical path: S1 → S4 → S5 (all gates blocked).

---

## Schedulability summary

| Slice | Status | Blocker | Owner | Unblocking meeting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | SCHEDULABLE | — | — | — |
| S2 | SCHEDULABLE | — | — | — |
| S3 | NOT SCHEDULABLE | BLK-02 | Legal | Legal/Product review (no date) |
| S4 | NOT SCHEDULABLE | BLK-05 | Platform Eng | Email capability review (no date) |
| S5 | NOT SCHEDULABLE | BLK-01 | Finance | Finance/Product experiment design review (no date) |

**Shipping strategy:** S1 and S2 can ship immediately. S3, S4, S5 require blocker resolution before scheduling.

**Narrow-first:** S2 (in-app) and S4 (email) launch US-only, prove the approach, then expand geographically. S3 (cancel) launches US-first, then per-market as BLK-02 resolves each market's requirements.

---

## Out of scope (orphaned candidates)

**Win-back discount in cancel flow** — wanted after demo, but cites nothing upstream. Held at the door by the judge: "does its source demand it, or merely permit it?" Goes upstream into a PR revision, or nowhere. Not in any slice.

**Proactive refunds for past charges** — awaiting BLK-03 decision. Not a requirement yet. Not in any slice.

---

stages.output:
# Readiness assessment — The Surprise Charge

## What this session does NOT know

### Claims without instrumentation
The press release makes claims this session cannot yet verify:
- **"85% reduction in surprise charges"** — no baseline Surprise Rate measured yet
- **"without hurting conversion"** — finance disputes this; no experiment designed
- **"one-tap cancel"** — regulatory feasibility unknown in all markets

### Requirements flagged
- **REQ-D2** (RESTS ON ASSUMPTION): The holdback experiment exists to measure the finance fear (C5), not settle it by fiat
- **REQ-D2, REQ-DP3** (SHAPE PENDING): Blocked on BLK-01 (experiment design), BLK-02 (per-market cancel flows)

### Slices — 2 schedulable, 2 blocked
| Slice | Status | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| R1 · Measure the fury | SCHEDULABLE | — |
| R2 · No-surprise surfaces | SCHEDULABLE | — |
| R3 · The reminder + experiment | BLOCKED | BLK-01, BLK-05 |
| R4 · One-tap cancel | BLOCKED | BLK-02 |

### Open questions that gate decisions
1. **What does the reminder cost in conversions?** (BLK-01) — finance won't ship without knowing; product won't defer without data proving the fear
2. **Which markets already require this?** (BLK-02) — shapes timeline, compliance risk, and whether one-tap is even ours to design
3. **Past charges: exposure and framing risk?** (BLK-03) — gates launch comms and possibly the "polite trial" framing
4. **How many users are silent-surprised?** (BLK-04) — refunders + ticketers measure anger, not impact
5. **Who owns send-before-charge ordering?** (BLK-05) — two vendors, no coordination layer

### Open blockers — 5 total
- 3 high severity: BLK-01 (commercial), BLK-02 (regulatory), BLK-03 (legal)
- 2 medium severity: BLK-04 (data), BLK-05 (dependency)
- All status: OPEN

---

## Recommendation

**GO WITH CONDITIONS** — for R1 and R2 only.

**R1 (Measure the fury)** and **R2 (No-surprise surfaces)** are unblocked and independently testable. Ship them. Both halves of the finance argument improve: product gets baseline Surprise Rate data (the demo cited none), finance gets honest receipts and in-app warnings that cost nothing and admit no new risk.

**R3 (The reminder + experiment)** and **R4 (One-tap cancel)** are **NOT YET DECIDABLE** — three high-severity blockers with no owners assigned, no meetings scheduled, no answers scoped. A GO that silently includes them answers BLK-01 (the commercial bet), BLK-02 (regulatory method), and BLK-03 (legal exposure) by assumption. Those belong to counsel, not a readiness doc.

**Scope of the GO**: R1 dark-ships instrumentation; R2 ships in-app banner and receipts to 100% of users. Neither surface requires email infra, vendor coordination, or regulatory pre-clearance. Both are reversible.

**Conditions**:
1. BLK-01 (finance experiment) gets an owner and one meeting within 5 business days, or R3 timeline slips
2. BLK-02 (regulatory scan) completes before R4 scoping — the answer shapes whether one-tap is ours to design or already prescribed
3. BLK-03 (legal exposure) resolves before launch comms — the "polite trial" framing may admit prior fault

---

## Blockers by severity

### High severity

**BLK-01 · COMMERCIAL**
- Ask: Finance fears reminders kill trial→paid conversion; product believes they don't. Neither has data. Will finance co-design the holdback experiment so the readout binds both sides?
- Owner role: finance lead (unassigned)
- Blocks: REQ-D2, R3
- Status: OPEN

## Assumptions that must hold

### A1 — The finance fear is resolvable by experiment
**Assumption**: A holdback experiment with binding readout terms will settle the conversion question, allowing both sides to defer to data.

**Breaks if false**: Finance refuses the experiment design, declares the risk unacceptable regardless of data, or disputes the readout methodology after seeing results.

**How to check**: BLK-01 resolution — one meeting with finance co-designing sample size, success criteria, and what result kills the reminder vs what result ships it.

### A2 — One-tap cancel is legally and technically feasible everywhere we operate
**Assumption**: No market we serve prescribes a cancel method incompatible with "one screen, one tap, inline confirmation."

**Breaks if false**: REQ-DP3 splinters into per-market flows; the parity rule (REQ-DP5) holds in some markets but not others; or worst case, a key market requires cancel-by-phone/mail, breaking the demo's core promise.

**How to check**: BLK-02 answer — compliance audit returning the public-category requirements (auto-renewal notice, click-to-cancel) and prescribed methods per market.

### A3 — The billing/email ordering is solvable
**Assumption**: A technical owner exists who can guarantee the reminder sends ≥48h before the charge, provably, across two vendors.

**Breaks if false**: REQ-DP1 is unshippable as written; the reminder becomes "best effort"; or the requirement downgrades to "within 48h" (which permits same-day, defeating the purpose).

**How to check**: BLK-05 resolution — platform lead either claims it or escalates to vendor contract renegotiation.

### A4 — Past charges create no launch-blocking liability
**Assumption**: Charges already taken from surprised users do not create exposure requiring proactive refunds, regulatory filings, or framing constraints that gut the "polite trial" narrative.

**Breaks if false**: Launch is delayed for remediation; the press release reframes from "innovation" to "compliance fix"; or worst case, BLK-03 answer is "don't launch until we've settled past claims."

**How to check**: BLK-03 answer from legal counsel.

## Top three reasons this fails (most likely first)

### 1. Finance vetoes the reminder, or the experiment shows conversion drop exceeds benefit
**Likelihood**: HIGH  
**Why most likely**: Finance's fear is the blocker with the longest lineage — it appears in IFAQ-01, blocks REQ-D2, and has no data on either side yet. Even if finance agrees to the experiment, the readout could show a conversion hit that finance deems unacceptable regardless of Surprise Rate improvement. This is a commercial bet with no technical fallback.

**Consequence**: R3 dies; the reminder never ships; the "polite trial" reduces to in-app banner + receipts (R2 only). Still better than the status quo, but the demo's headline claim (the reminder) is gone.

**Early signal**: Finance declines the experiment meeting (BLK-01), or agrees but sets success criteria product can't meet ("no measurable conversion drop").

---

### 2. Regulatory requirements in key markets demand a different implementation than the demo
**Likelihood**: MEDIUM-HIGH  
**Why second**: BLK-02 is unscoped — compliance hasn't confirmed which markets already require what we're designing, or which prescribe the cancel method. If a major market (e.g., EU, CA, UK) requires cancel-by-phone or a multi-step confirmation flow, REQ-DP3 and REQ-DP5 (the parity rule) fracture into per-market variants. The demo assumed one global flow.

**Consequence**: One-tap cancel (R4) splinters; the simple demo promise ("one screen, one tap, everywhere") downgrades to "one tap in most markets, prescribed flow in others." Or best case, BLK-02 answer accelerates timeline in markets where "already required."

**Early signal**: Compliance memo returns markets with cancel-method prescriptions incompatible with one-tap.

---

### 3. The billing/email ordering guarantee proves technically or contractually unsolvable
**Likelihood**: MEDIUM  
**Why third**: BLK-05 is scoped as "who owns it" rather than "is it possible" — suggests the path exists but ownership is unclear. However, if the billing vendor and email queue are contractually or architecturally decoupled, guaranteeing send-before-charge may require vendor renegotiation, a new coordination service, or downgrading the requirement to "best effort."

**Consequence**: REQ-DP1 (the T-48h reminder) ships with weaker ordering semantics, or doesn't ship at all. The experiment (REQ-D2, R3) may still run, but the reminder's reliability promise is compromised.

**Early signal**: Platform lead (BLK-05 owner) declares no existing owner and no technical layer to enforce ordering.
